correctness.rationale: Independently proved the table without extrapolation or executing the frozen scripts. A residual fixes the parity of every deletion gap (initial, between surviving letters, and terminal) because the host alternates and both endpoints are prescribed. For the empty residual there is just one odd gap. Three deletions therefore give either three odd gaps, all singletons, or one odd gap. With three odd gaps the embedding is unique, and counting isolated deletion positions reduces to three nonnegative slack variables: the first position starts at 1+u1, the minimal successive distances are 2+[u1≠u2] and 2+[u2≠u3], and the last allowable position is the largest index of parity carrying u3. Increments come in twos. With one odd gap q (number of retained letters before it), the base pattern is the bit b=q mod 2. The extra pair can be in q (giving b,1−b,b), in an earlier gap j<q (giving j mod 2, its opposite, b), or in a later gap j>q (giving b, (j+1) mod 2, its opposite). Count distinct q, not the positions of the extra pair. In order 000,001,010,011,100,101,110,111 the one-odd-gap counts are (0,n−1,n−1,n−1,n−2,n−1,n−2,0) on E_n and (0,n−1,n,n−1,n−1,n−1,n−1,0) on O_n. Adding the isolated counts gives the stated 16 polynomials via Pascal, including O_1 and E_2. Multiplying the resulting binomial series by (1−z)^4 gives the frozen numerators, and subtracting the indicated rows gives the unit gaps. The frozen interleaving DFA and Cayley–Hamilton certificate also correctly distinguish residuals from embeddings.

For 100 and 110 the leading 0 and trailing 1 are both forced retained; trim both and complement to obtain E_(n−1) with 011 or 001, respectively. For 010 use the alternating-prefix theorem with d=3; reverse-complement gives 101 on the same E_n.

Odd host: for 001 and 011 the terminal 0 is forced retained, so trim to E_n. Reverse the palindromic O_n to cover 100 and 110. For 010 use d=3 directly. For 101 both end zeros are forced retained; trim and complement to O_(n−1) with pattern 010 (n=1 has no such embedding).
For 000 or 111, every chosen triple among positions carrying the bit has a distinct residual because the opposite bit survives at every separator. This gives the constant-pattern binomials directly.
